cards.explanation: The answer is True. The writer says, "it is fitting for the upright to praise Him." Fitting means it suits them, the way this tall white hat suits me. Rejoicing and praising come in the same breath here, friends (Ps 33:1).
The answer is False. Verse 3 says, "Sing to Him a new song; play skillfully with a shout of joy." So the harp and ten strings come with a shout, friends. Nobody is told to whisper this one (Ps 33:3).

The answer is False. The writer says the word of the LORD is upright, and "…all His work is trustworthy." There's no fine print and no exceptions in that line, friends. Every bit of it can be trusted (Ps 33:4).

The answer is His loving devotion. Verse 5 says, "the earth is full of His loving devotion." Full, like a cookie box packed to the lid, friends. After hearing that the LORD loves righteousness and justice, this is where the writer lands (Ps 33:5).

The answer is the breath of His mouth. Verse 6 says, "By the word of the LORD the heavens were made, and all the stars by the breath of His mouth." Every star in the sky, and it all came from His breath. Meanwhile I need an oven and a timer to make a single star-shaped cookie, friends (Ps 33:6).

The answer is False. Verse 8 says, "Let all the earth fear the LORD; let all the people of the world revere Him." The writer doesn't narrow it to one people, friends. It's everybody on the earth (Ps 33:8).

The answer is that He frustrates them. Verse 10 says, "The LORD frustrates the plans of the nations; He thwarts the devices of the peoples." The writer says it twice, once with each word, friends. I've watched my own plans fall flat, but this is a whole different scale (Ps 33:10).
The word is forever. Verse 11 says, "The counsel of the LORD stands forever…" Plans of the nations come and go, friends, but His doesn't. I'd call that a pretty good contrast (Ps 33:11).

The answer is the nation whose God is the LORD. Verse 12 says, "Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD, the people He has chosen as His inheritance!" The blessing goes to the nation that belongs to Him, friends. That's the one the writer calls blessed (Ps 33:12).

The answer is all the sons of men. Verse 13 says, "The LORD looks down from heaven; He sees all the sons of men." All of them, friends, from the top to the very back of the line. Nobody gets lost in the crowd (Ps 33:13).

The answer is False. The psalm says He shapes the hearts of each, and He "…considers all their works." So He doesn't ignore what people do, friends. It comes right after He shapes the hearts of each (Ps 33:15).

The answer is False. The psalm says, "No king is saved by his vast army; no warrior is delivered by his great strength." A king can have all the soldiers he wants, and it's still not what saves him. The writer says it plainly, friends, and I like how plain it is (Ps 33:16).

The answer is a vain hope. Verse 17 says, "A horse is a vain hope for salvation; even its great strength cannot save." The horse has great strength, and the writer still says it can't save, friends. Strength just isn't the thing doing the rescuing (Ps 33:17).

The two words are fear and hope. Verse 18 says, "Surely the eyes of the LORD are on those who fear Him…" It's the same word the psalm used back in verse 8 when it called all the earth to fear Him. Then the verse says, "…on those whose hope is in His loving devotion" Notice where the hope sits, friends: not in armies or horses, but in His loving devotion. The verse before it said armies and horses can't save, and here is where hope belongs (Ps 33:16–18).

The answer is to deliver them from death. Verse 19 says His eyes are on them "…to deliver them from death and keep them alive in famine." It's a rescue, not a rating, friends. His eyes are on them for the sake of saving them (Ps 33:19).

The answer is their help and their shield. Verse 20 says, "He is our help and our shield." Help for when they need a hand, a shield for when they need cover, friends. And all of it happens while their soul is waiting (Ps 33:20).

The answer is True. Verse 21 says, "For our hearts rejoice in Him, since we trust in His holy name." The rejoicing and the trusting go together, friends. And it circles back to the rejoicing the psalm opened with (Ps 33:21).
